profiles.summary: Arbitrum One still answers as nitro v3.13.0-rc.9+b72783f on go1.27.3 (arm64) at ArbOS 61, and the cycle 23 reruns match the specification. New this cycle: the release image of the same commit was read at binary level, which ties the running code to a go-ethereum v1.17.x based fork and to holiman/uint256 v1.3.2, and the compiled integer and opcode functions of both architectures were scanned for the open Go compiler fault shapes.

deltas.delta: The Nitro build that the Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain endpoints report (v3.13.0-rc.9+b72783f, go1.27.3) is the same commit as the binary-only v3.13.0 release published on 25 November 2026 as offchainlabs/nitro-node:v3.13.0-b72783f-stripped. The Go build information read from the amd64 and arm64 nitro binaries of that image (without running them) pins holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 with the same h1 hash as the public Nitro go.sum, and replaces go-ethereum with a local directory. The function table of the binary shows a go-ethereum fork that is newer than the f1c5f02 fork earlier cycles read: it contains upstream go-ethereum v1.17.x code (the shared stack arena with pop1Peek1 and pop2Peek1, the GasBudget type of EIP-8037, a precompile result cache, handlers for EIP-8024 and EIP-7843, and an Amsterdam instruction set). Every arithmetic, comparison, shift, BYTE, KECCAK256, CALLDATALOAD and RETURNDATACOPY handler starts exactly 4 lines later than in go-ethereum v1.17.7, consistent with identical bodies under a longer import block.

The compiled code of 53 functions (holiman/uint256 Add, Sub, Mul, Div, Mod, SDiv, SMod, MulMod, AddMod, Exp, Lsh, Rsh, SRsh, Byte, ExtendSign, Slt, Sgt, Lt, Gt, Eq, IsZero, udivrem, udivremKnuth, udivremBy1, umul, and core/vm opDiv to opSAR, opKeccak256, opCallDataLoad, opMcopy, opTload, opTstore, opJump, opJumpi, Contract.validJumpdest, Contract.isCode and codeBitmapInternal) was located through the binary's pclntab and disassembled for amd64 and arm64. On amd64 there are 13 carry masks (sbb r,r) and none has its flags read by a SETcc, CMOVcc, Jcc, ADC or SBB before another flag write. On arm64 there is no condition code mi, pl, vs or vc (the noov lowering) and no 32 bit REV; the only REV instructions are 64 bit ones in opTload and opTstore. The jump destination analysis compares only against PUSH1 (0x60) and the push widths, as in the source.

Nitro v3.13.0 was announced on 25 November 2026 as a binary-only release whose source follows later. It changes how eth_sendRawTransaction and eth_sendRawTransactionSync respond (earlier return, partial receipts that can be retracted) and ships no consensus machine newer than consensus-v61: the image's machines/latest link points to 0xc10cd7ec...dc97.

profiles.summary: Nothing new on transient storage or transaction boundaries. The multi-step swap replay of this cycle could not read historical state from the public Arbitrum One endpoint (25 of 25 refused), so no new replay evidence for Arbitrum One.

Native token management and transaction filtering are still off (both getters return zero at block 527,629,490). The Glamsterdam L1 pricing proposal changes only parentGasFloorPerToken and perBatchGasCharge and is gated on Glamsterdam reaching Ethereum.

No ArbOS upgrade is scheduled (getScheduledUpgrade() returns zeros at block 527,629,490). The precompile result cache in the new fork serves only stock pure precompiles; no ArbOS precompile implements the opt-in interface.

deltas.delta: The rc.9 fork carries go-ethereum's precompile result cache (core/vm/precompile_cache.go, first in v1.17.6). In the v3.13.0 binary the only types with a Cacheable method are the twenty stock precompiles (ecrecover, sha256, ripemd160, modexp, the bn256 and BLS12-381 families, blake2F, point evaluation, p256Verify); none of Nitro's ArbOS precompiles has one, so no stateful precompile answer is replayed from the cache.

profiles.summary: Robinhood Chain answers as the same rc.9 build on both amd64 and arm64, and the cycle 23 reruns match. The binary-level reading of the v3.13.0 image of the same commit covers both of its architectures.

It lists no zero-value frame, so unlock, take of tokens, mint and burn frames are absent and the nesting question of L-1004 cannot be answered from it.
HYPE remains the native gas token; native token management and transaction filtering are off at block 10,894,422.
The HyperCore read precompile and CoreWriter predeploy are still not scheduled (getScheduledUpgrade() returns zeros at block 10,894,422, arbOSVersion 116).

findings.title: Nitro v3.13.0 carries dormant Amsterdam execution rules that a future ArbOS version would switch on, and the PoolManager bytecode has no instruction they reinterpret
findings.difference: Ethereum has not scheduled Glamsterdam. The Nitro build that the Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain endpoints run (commit b72783f, published as the v3.13.0 binary-only image on 25 November 2026) already contains a go-ethereum v1.17.x based interpreter with an Amsterdam instruction set (newAmsterdamInstructionSet and newArbitrumAmsterdamInstructionSet in its function table), the EIP-8037 two-part gas budget (GasBudget with ChargeState, ChargeExecution and Forward; Contract.forwardGas and refundState), handlers for the EIP-8024 opcodes (opDupN, opSwapN, opExchange) and EIP-7843 (opSlotNum). These rules switch on only with an ArbOS version that the chain owner schedules; at ArbOS 61 the endpoints run the Osaka set and no upgrade is scheduled on either chain.
findings.mechanism: Two parts of the PoolManager meet these rules. First, the bytecode: walked instruction by instruction, the 24,009 byte PoolManager on Arbitrum One has no byte 0x1e, 0x4b, 0xe6, 0xe7 or 0xe8 at an instruction position and no other opcode that is undefined today; the only 0xfe is the trailing invalid at offset 23,996. So no branch of the PoolManager would decode differently when DUPN, SWAPN, EXCHANGE or SLOTNUM become valid, and the compiled jump destination analysis of the binary treats only PUSH1 to PUSH32 as carrying immediates, as in go-ethereum v1.17.7 analysis_legacy.go. Second, gas: under EIP-8037 the GAS opcode returns only the execution part of the budget, and state creation is paid from a separate reservoir. The PoolManager forwards gas() on three calls: the native payout (src/types/Currency.sol:48), the token transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:73) and the hook call (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134). In go-ethereum v1.17.7 opCall hands the callee its execution gas plus the caller's whole state reservoir (NewGasBudget(gas, scope.Contract.Gas.StateGas)), so a callee that creates state may draw on a reservoir the caller sized for itself. The outcome of a call is still decided only by success and return data (Currency.sol:48-52 and 73-79, Hooks.sol:134-160), and the PoolManager's own writes are storage updates of existing pools, positions and claims, so the rule can change which transactions run out of gas, not what a successful call computes or who is debited.
findings.impact: No funds move. Once an ArbOS version enables these rules, a transaction that creates many new storage slots (first position in a pool, first ERC-6909 claim balance, first tick of a range) needs more total gas; that is a pricing change of the A9 kind, recorded for the deployment checklist.
findings.preconditions: The chain owner (ArbitrumDAO for Arbitrum One, the two chain owners for Robinhood Chain) must schedule an ArbOS version that activates the Amsterdam rules. No such version is proposed: the v3.13.0 image ships no consensus machine newer than consensus-v61, and getScheduledUpgrade() returns zeros on both chains on 26 November 2026.
findings.mitigations: Before any ArbOS upgrade that names Glamsterdam features, rerun battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py and pmdiff2.py against the upgraded Sepolia or a block time override, and rerun the gas-capped scripts (pmdiff2 script 189) to see which liquidity operations change gas class.

cleared.check: Whether the build behind the rc.9 endpoints pins a holiman/uint256 revision other than v1.3.2, read from the Go build information of the v3.13.0-b72783f release binaries for amd64 and arm64 (parsed with scripts/gobuildinfo.py, not executed).
cleared.result: Both binaries pin github.com/holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 with h1:a9EgMPSC1AAaj1SZL5zIQD3WbwTuHrMGOerLjGmM/TA=, the hash in the public Nitro master and v3.12.4 go.sum, and were built with go1.27.3, trimpath and CGO. The unreleased uint256 master rewrite of Div, SDiv, Slt and the modular routines is therefore not in the running code, so the FullMath divisions by powers of two (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:62, 67, 73) and the SDIV and SLT of TickBitmap.compress (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:24-26) run the v1.3.2 paths that earlier cycles tested.

cleared.check: Compiled-code check on the release binaries of commit b72783f for the open Go fault shapes of F-143: amd64 carry masks whose flags feed a flag reader (issue 82825), arm64 noov conditions and 32 bit REV folds, across 53 integer library and opcode functions located through pclntab (runtime.text 0x45d7c0 on amd64, 0x453e50 on arm64).
cleared.result: amd64: 13 sbb r,r carry masks in uint256 udivrem, Div, Mod and related functions; none has its flags read by SETcc, CMOVcc, Jcc, ADC or SBB before the next flag write. arm64: no mi, pl, vs or vc condition and no 32 bit REV in any of the 53 functions; the 12 REV instructions are 64 bit, in opTload and opTstore. So Lsh, Rsh, SRsh and opSHL, opSHR, opSAR, which compute TickMath.getSqrtPriceAtTick (src/libraries/TickMath.sol:61-111) and the BitMath scans (src/libraries/BitMath.sol:16-45), contain none of these shapes in compiled form on either architecture. Limit: the binaries are the release build of the same commit, not the running files, and functions inlined into other packages were not scanned.

cleared.check: Arithmetic and stack semantics of the go-ethereum v1.17.x code inside the rc.9 fork: pointer-returning pops (pop1Peek1, pop2Peek1) with the result written into an operand slot, the shared stack arena across call frames, and the opcode handlers' line alignment with go-ethereum v1.17.7.
cleared.result: All 42 arithmetic, comparison, shift, BYTE, SIGNEXTEND, EXP, KECCAK256, CALLDATALOAD and copy handlers start 4 lines after their v1.17.7 counterparts, and stack.go function lines match v1.17.4 to v1.17.9 exactly. In v1.17.7 the aliasing of receiver and operand (z.MulMod(x, y, z), z.AddMod(x, y, z), exponent.Exp(base, exponent), num.ExtendSign(num, back)) is the same aliasing the older handlers had, and opCall copies all seven arguments by value before the child frame reuses the arena. The 185,529 battery and targeted vectors run through these handlers and match.

cleared.check: Whether future instruction sets in the running node (EIP-8024 DUPN, SWAPN, EXCHANGE at 0xe6 to 0xe8, EIP-7843 SLOTNUM at 0x4b, CLZ at 0x1e) could change how the deployed PoolManager decodes.
cleared.result: The deployed PoolManager has none of these bytes at an instruction position and no undefined opcode other than the trailing 0xfe at offset 23,996, so their activation cannot change a branch or a jump destination in it.

cleared.check: Whether the precompile result cache added with the v1.17.x merge can replay an answer of a stateful ArbOS precompile to a PoolManager take, sync or hook call.
cleared.result: RunPrecompiledContract consults the cache only when precompileCacheKey accepts the precompile, which needs the opt-in Cacheable method. In the v3.13.0 binary only the twenty stock pure precompiles have that method. ArbSys, ArbRetryableTx and the other ArbOS precompiles always execute. The PoolManager itself calls no precompile; only a caller-chosen take target or hook address could be one.

cleared.check: Effect of the Nitro v3.13.0 change to eth_sendRawTransaction and eth_sendRawTransactionSync on PoolManager settlement.
cleared.result: The change is in RPC responses only: a returned partial receipt can be retracted if the block is not sealed. Settlement is atomic inside one transaction (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114), so core is unaffected; integrations that release funds on a sync receipt fall under A14.

cleared.check: Scheduled ArbOS upgrades, chain owners, filtering and native token management on 26 November 2026, and the consensus machines shipped with v3.13.0.
cleared.result: getScheduledUpgrade() returns zeros on all three chains, arbOSVersion is 116 (ArbOS 61) everywhere, native token management is off everywhere, transaction filtering is on only on Robinhood Chain (F-001). The v3.13.0 image ships module roots 0x2c54f6e9, 0x8a7513bf, 0xc10cd7ec and 0xc2c02df5 with latest pointing to 0xc10cd7ec (consensus-v61), so the release prepares no new state transition function.

leads.question: When the full source of Nitro v3.13.0 (commit b72783f) is published, does its go-ethereum submodule equal go-ethereum v1.17.7 plus the Arbitrum files in core/vm instructions.go, stack.go, interpreter.go and contract.go, and does opCall at ArbOS 61 build the child budget from the forwarded execution gas only?
leads.why: This cycle tied the running code to v1.17.x by function line numbers in the binary, not by reading the fork's text, and the EIP-8037 reservoir hand-off changes what a hook or token callee can spend.

leads.question: Which public Arbitrum One endpoint serves historical state for the 25 newest multi-step swaps, so that replay.py can run on this chain again?
leads.why: replay.py could not replay any Arbitrum One multi-step swap this cycle; the last whole-loop replays are from cycle 18.

leadResults.answer: Only the Elysium half is in this unit. The Etherscan-style API at elysium.kinetiq.xyz/explorer/api serves txlistinternal for the PoolManager in block windows of up to about 15,000 blocks (full history times out) and includes frames whose parent reverted, but it lists only frames that carry value: in blocks 10,850,000 to 10,895,000 it returned 5,780 frames (2,461 settle calls with value, 3,319 native payouts) and no zero-value frame. Unlock frames therefore never appear, so the absence of an unlock frame above a settle says nothing, and the question needs a trace endpoint. Arcscan (5042) belongs to another unit.

The rc.9 build b72783f was released on 25 November 2026 as the binary-only offchainlabs/nitro-node:v3.13.0-b72783f-stripped image. Its amd64 and arm64 nitro binaries pin holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 with the public go.sum hash, are built with go1.27.3, and replace go-ethereum with a local directory. The function table shows a go-ethereum fork with v1.17.x code (stack arena, EIP-8037 GasBudget, precompile cache, EIP-8024 and EIP-7843 handlers); the arithmetic and comparison handlers start 4 lines after go-ethereum v1.17.7's. The uint256 pin is unchanged and the core/vm changes are the upstream v1.17.x ones, which the battery, targeted set and both script sets exercise without mismatch. The exact fork commit is not stated in the binary.

No Elysium mainnet image or commit is published. Kinetiq's documentation says the chain runs stock ArbOS 61 with Conduit; the only public node package (Enigma-Validator/elysium-rpc-node) is for the testnet and pins nitro-node v3.9.5-66e42c4, and Hypedexer's mainnet endpoint refuses unauthenticated calls. The build stays tested through its answers only, which match on every rerun this cycle.

No Nitro release has moved past v1.3.2 yet: the v3.13.0-b72783f binaries released on 25 November 2026 and the public master go.mod still pin holiman/uint256 v1.3.2. The u256diff harness has nothing new to run against until a release pins a later revision.

No request feature ties an answer to an architecture: responses carry only Cloudflare and Envoy headers with no backend identifier, and six consecutive calls alternated between arm64 and amd64. Instead the compiled integer and opcode functions of both architectures' release binaries of the same commit were scanned (see L-962), which covers the architecture question without pinning calls.

For the Nitro builds of Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain: a compiled check of the go1.27.3 release binaries of commit b72783f for amd64 and arm64 covered uint256 Lsh, Rsh, SRsh, the division and modular routines, and core/vm opSHL, opSHR, opSAR and the other arithmetic handlers. On amd64 none of the 13 SBB carry masks has its flags read by SETcc, CMOVcc, Jcc, ADC or SBB before the next flag write; on arm64 there is no noov condition (mi, pl, vs, vc) and no 32 bit REV. Which client builds adopt a Go release carrying the five fixes is still open for the other networks of this lead, and Elysium (go1.25.12) was not part of this check.

Operator level. No public challenger or watchtower for Robinhood Chain or Elysium was found, and no batch replay was run; the v3.13.0 image confirms that consensus-v61 (0xc10cd7ec...dc97) is still the latest machine shipped, and the Elysium build's source is still unnamed.
